subproblem.title: Localization of integrals of functions continuous on an open set and vanishing off a compact subset
subproblem.statement: Let n be a natural number; integrals are Bochner integrals for Lebesgue measure on R^n. Let f : R^n -> R, and let O and T be subsets of R^n such that O is open, T is compact and T is contained in O. Assume that f is continuous on O (as a map restricted to O) and that f(z) = 0 for every z not in T. Then (a) f is continuous on all of R^n, (b) f is Lebesgue integrable on R^n, and (c) the integral of f over O equals the integral of f over R^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Rn n → ℝ) (O T : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen O → IsCompact T → T ⊆ O → ContinuousOn f O → (∀ z, z ∉ T → f z = 0) → Continuous f ∧ Integrable f ∧ ∫ z in O, f z = ∫ z, f z
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3c of the parent proof (the lemma stated there), written out in full. Let mu denote Lebesgue measure on R^n (MeasureTheory.volume); all integrals are Bochner integrals for mu.
1. T is closed. R^n is a Hausdorff space, so the compact set T is closed (IsCompact.isClosed). Hence the complement of T is open.
2. Continuity at points of O. Let z be in O. Since O is open, O is a neighbourhood of z (IsOpen.mem_nhds), so the continuity of f on O gives continuity of f at z (ContinuousOn.continuousAt).
3. Continuity at points outside O. Let z be outside O. Then z is not in T, because T is contained in O. By step 1, the complement W of T is an open neighbourhood of z, and f(w) = 0 for every w in W by hypothesis. So f agrees with the constant function 0 on a neighbourhood of z, and f is continuous at z (continuousAt_const.congr applied to this eventual equality).
4. Claim (a). By steps 2 and 3, f is continuous at every point of R^n, hence continuous (continuous_iff_continuousAt). Equivalently: tsupport f is contained in the closed set T, hence in the open set O, and ContinuousOn.continuous_of_tsupport_subset applies.
5. Compact support. f(z) = 0 for every z outside the compact set T, so the support of f lies in T and its closure tsupport f lies in the closed set T. Hence tsupport f is a closed subset of a compact set, i.e. f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro).
6. Claim (b). A continuous function with compact support is integrable for every measure that is finite on compact sets, and Lebesgue measure is such a measure. So f is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport, using steps 4 and 5).
7. Claim (c). If z is not in O, then z is not in T, since T is contained in O; so f(z) = 0. Thus f vanishes on the complement of O, and the integral of f over O equals the integral of f over R^n (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
8. Steps 4, 6 and 7 prove (a), (b) and (c). QED.
proof_key_steps: T is compact in the Hausdorff space R^n, hence closed
f is continuous at each point of the open set O; a point outside O lies in the open complement of T, where f = 0, so f is continuous there too
f vanishes outside the compact set T, so it has compact support and, being continuous, is integrable
f vanishes outside O, so its integral over O equals its integral over R^n

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose and includes every hypothesis. Closedness of T supplies the zero neighbourhoods outside O; continuity inside O uses openness. Support containment yields compact support and integrability, and vanishing outside O gives the integral identity. All three conclusions follow without circular reliance, including when T is empty.
